memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'On the day you wave the sheaf, you must sacrifice as a burnt offering
to the LORD a lamb a year old without defect, together with its grain
offering of two-tenths of an ephah of the finest flour mixed with olive
oil - a food offering presented to the LORD, a pleasing aroma - and its
drink offering of a quarter of a hin of wine. You must not eat any
bread, or roasted or new grain, until the very day you bring this
offering to your God. This is to be a lasting ordinance for the
generations to come, wherever you live'" - Lev 23:12-14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The instruction is firm: eat nothing from the new harvest until the
offering has been made. After a long winter, with fresh grain finally
standing in the field, a hungry family had to wait.

Why? Because God was teaching them where the harvest came from. It
would have been easy, after months of ploughing and sowing and
weeding, to feel that the crop was simply the product of hard work.
The offering interrupted that thought before it could take root.

Dear friend, Moses later warned Israel about exactly this danger - that
when they had eaten and were satisfied, they would say in their heart,
"My power and the strength of my hands have produced this wealth"
(Deut 8:17). It is a very human drift.

Every good and perfect gift is from above (Jas 1:17). Paul asks
bluntly: what do you have that you did not receive (1 Cor 4:7)?

This is not to diminish honest hard work. It is to keep gratitude
alive alongside it. You worked, yes. But who gave the strength, the
rain, the seed, the years?

Put God first in what you receive, before appetite takes over.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I quietly credit myself for what God has provided?
2. What is the "first portion" God is asking me to offer Him?
3. How can I build gratitude into the moment I receive, not after?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, everything I have came from Your hand. Guard me from taking
credit for Your gifts, and teach me to give You the first place. Amen.
